title: A Tiny Cat Mistaken for a Pet Was Actually a New Wild Species
mediaSource: Leopardus tilcayo Bolivia Yungas new wild cat species tiger cat

scenes.title: A strange little pet turned out to be a new wild cat species
scenes.narration: A tiny cat once taken in by a Bolivian family has been identified as a wild feline species new to science.

scenes.title: Its name is the tilcayo
scenes.narration: Leopardus tilcayo lives in Bolivia's Yungas cloud forest and is the first living wild cat species formally described in more than a century.

scenes.title: It is smaller than an average house cat
scenes.narration: The known male measures about 46 centimeters long and weighs roughly 1.4 kilograms, making it unusually small for a wild cat.

scenes.title: Genomes revealed it was truly different
scenes.narration: Researchers compared tiger cat genomes across South America and found that the tilcayo belongs to a distinct evolutionary lineage.

scenes.title: Its known range is still tiny
scenes.narration: So far the species has only been confirmed in the Bolivian Yungas, and scientists still know very little about its population, behavior, and full range.

scenes.title: Even cats still hold unknown species
scenes.narration: Cats are among the world's most familiar animals, yet a new wild species was still hiding in a cloud forest.
